titulo: Layered architecture revisited with the state as of Oct 2026
lead: A site ready for agents is not an API: it is eight layers, from the ones that describe the site to the ones that protect it. The WebMCP track already had this map; here it comes back with the status of each layer as of 10/19/2026 and a script that searches your code for the evidence of each one.
objetivo: review the 8 layers with the 10/19/2026 status and find the evidence for each one in the code, in the kit and in your project.

aprende.t: The 8 layers and what each one answers
What is stable and what is a draft as of 10/19/2026
Search the code for evidence of each layer
Which course in the track owns each layer

hero_alt: A stack of eight thin plates of dark glass with metal spacers on a desk, with a blurred monitor in the background.

secoes.titulo: The 8 layers, from bottom to top
secoes.sub: The first four describe the site; the last four protect it. Click each one.

nos.detalhe: robots.txt, sitemap, structured data. Stable. llms.txt is a proposal with no measured effect on citations. Owner: inemaSEO Track.
document.modelContext.registerTool: Community Group draft from 10/16/2026, origin trial in Chrome 149 to 156. The form as a tool was left out of the spec. Owner: course 2.
Name, description and JSON Schema that state the real effect. Stable practice, valid in WebMCP and in MCP. Owners: courses 1 and 2.
A rule error comes back as data ({ erro }), so the agent can fix it. In Chromium 156, a throw arrives only as UnknownError. Owner: course 2.
An action with consequences waits for the person. Confirmation is stable practice; the consequentialHint annotation is a draft. Owners: courses 2 and 4.
By default, only the site's own origin sees the tool; exposedTo and iframes are a draft (course 4). The approved catalog with autonomy level is lesson 7.
The rule lives in one place and serves the screen, WebMCP and MCP. MCP at revision 2026-07-28, stable. Course 1 and lesson 2 of this course.
Call log, frozen battery, spec watcher and report: lessons 3, 4, 6 and 8. Evals in depth: LOOP-R Engenharia.

secoes.legenda: Structure of the WebMCP track (§04), with the status re-read in the spec, in Chrome Status and in MCP as of 10/19/2026.

secoes.titulo: What changed from the old map
secoes.sub: The area had the right layers; four labels went stale.

texto: The old map put "declarative, from forms" tools side by side with the imperative ones.
As of 10/16/2026 the declarative API is out of the spec: only Chrome implements it, in the trial. Experimental as of 10/19/2026.
llms.txt showed up as an item to publish.
Today it is a proposal with no measured effect on citations. The decision to publish stays with the inemaSEO Track.
The MCP side of the old track predated the 2026-07-28 revision.
Now: no initialize and no session, server/discover and confirmation by MRTR.
Before, the layers went to phases (Builder, Integrator, Agent Developer, Expert).
Now they go to the 6 courses by topic; the script shows the owner of each layer.

exemplo.texto: Status with a date. If the date has gone stale, reread the source before trusting it.

secoes.titulo: Look for the evidence for each layer
secoes.sub: camadas.mjs reads the files in the folder (without node_modules) and looks for a sign of each layer. It measures presence, not quality.

Each line says where it found the sign, the status of the layer as of 10/19/2026, and the owner course.

Running it in a folder without the code (the build folder, an empty folder) gives 0/8 and exit 1. The criterion fails before the work does: that is how it counts as proof.

secoes.sub: The kit first, then your project. Each exercise ends with a done when.

exercicios.titulo: E1 · The layers in the kit
exercicios.texto: Install the kit (lesson 2, install block) and run the layers block.

exercicios.pronto: The block prints CAMADAS: 0/8 com evidência and saída: 1.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · The layers of your project
exercicios.texto: Run the script in your site's folder and note, for each layer marked "falta", the lesson or course that fixes it.
exercicios.pronto: node scripts/camadas.mjs [your site's folder] prints the line CAMADAS: N/8 com evidência, and the file camadas-[your site].md has one line for each missing layer.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after the answer.

perguntas.p: On 10/19/2026, which of these layers is a draft and not a stable practice?
opcoes: Confirm with the person before an action with consequences.
Register tools with document.modelContext on the page.
Describe the tool with a name, a description, and a JSON Schema.
Serve the same rule through the MCP server on the 2026-07-28 revision.
perguntas.explica: document.modelContext is a Community Group draft (10/16/2026), with an origin trial in Chrome 149–156. Confirmation and the contract are stable practices; MCP 2026-07-28 is the current revision.

perguntas.p: The script scored 8/8 on your project. What does that prove?
opcoes: That the site is ready for production and protected against injection.
That the tools work in your visitors' browsers.
That the code has a signal for each layer, not that the quality is good.
That the site will show up more in AI answers.
perguntas.explica: camadas.mjs measures the presence of evidence. Working is the battery (lesson 4); security is course 4; showing up in AIs belongs to the inemaSEO Track and is not an effect of WebMCP.

perguntas.p: The old map listed tools as "declarative, from forms." What changed?
opcoes: They are outside the 10/16/2026 spec; only Chrome implements them, in the trial.
They became the official way and replaced registerTool.
They were removed from Chrome in the 149–156 origin trial.
They now require an MCP server to work.
perguntas.explica: The declarative API is under "Future Exploration… not part of the specification" and in a separate explainer; Chrome documents and implements it in the trial. Experimental as of 10/19/2026.

perguntas.p: In which layer does the decision to publish llms.txt sit?
opcoes: Tools, because the agent reads the file as a tool.
Evals, because the file measures the agent's performance.
Permissions, because the file says who can call.
Discovery, with the decision in the inemaSEO Track.
perguntas.explica: llms.txt is discovery: a public file. It is a proposal with no measured effect on citations; the inemaSEO Track decides and teaches it.

itens.texto: Four describe the site, four protect it; none alone means "ready for agents."
Each layer has a status with a date: draft, proposal, or stable as of 10/19/2026.
camadas.mjs finds the signal for each layer in the code; proof that it works comes in the next lessons.
